Theme

Latin word

quō

quō (+ comparative and subjunctive)

conjunction, where the clause has a comparative · Wiktionary

so that (the more …); where (to)? whither?

In this lexicon

  • so that

    also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 5.97: respondisse sē, quō melius cēnāret, obsōnāre ambulandō famem

  • where to

    the recommended word · classical · Plaut. Amph. 341: Quō ambulās tū?; Hor. S. 1.9.62–63: unde venīs et quō tendis?; Traupman 406

  • vinculum quō duae fistulae conjunguntur: coupler

    * our formation

  • vehiculum onerārium quō harēna effunditur: dump truck

    * our formation

  • Quid prō quō.: quid pro quo

    Renaissance

  • ex quō fit ut: result

    classical

  • ex quō (tempore): since

    classical

  • nesciō quō modō (nesciō quōmodo): somehow

    classical

  • quō locō rēs est?: state

    classical

  • quō … eō (+ comparative): the more …, the more …

    classical

Examples

  • Sōcratēn ferunt … respondisse sē, quō melius cēnāret, obsōnāre ambulandō famem

    they say Socrates answered that he was buying in hunger by walking, so as to dine betterCic. Tusc. 5.97

    In the entry for so that

  • Quō ambulās tū?

    Where are you off to?Plaut. Amph. 341

    In the entry for where to

  • unde venīs et quō tendis?

    where have you come from, and where are you heading?Hor. S. 1.9.62–63

    In the entry for where to

  • Quō abīs? manē; manē, inquam: quō abīs?

    Where are you going? Wait; wait, I tell you: where are you going?Ter. Hec. 495–496

    In the entry for where to

  • Abī deambulātum. — Deambulātum quō? — Vah! quasi dēsit locus.

    Go for a walk. — A walk where? — Pah! As if there were nowhere to go.Ter. Haut. 587

    In the entry for where to

  • nesciō hercle, neque unde eam, neque quōrsum eam

    I really don’t know where I’m coming from or where I’m goingTer. Eun. 304
